title: API & SDK: pin-resolution audit trail and client-side validation for model pins
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Teams onboard models and pin by tag/semver/commit-hash, but production incidents show confusing resolution behavior, silent fallbacks, and no clear audit trail tying requests to the resolved model+performance profile. Goal: introduce a deterministic resolution algorithm with explicit precedence rules, an immutable audit trace that travels with requests/responses, and client-side validation helpers in SDKs to prevent accidental pins that violate policy or are timebound. Scope: API surface additions for pin metadata and audit_id, SDK validation layers, updates to the pin-resolver service, backwards-compatible runtime behavior, and migration path for existing pinned routes.
acceptance_criteria: API accepts optional pin metadata fields (pin_type, pin_value, pin_hint) and returns resolved_model_ref + pin_audit_id in responses
SDKs (Python/TS) expose helpers to validate pin formats (tag, semver range, hash) and to detect potential ambiguity before the call
Resolver precedence documented and implemented: explicit commit-hash > exact semver > semver-range > immutable tag > alias (experimental)
Each resolution emits an immutable pin_audit_id that can be used to retrieve human-readable audit entries from the control plane for 90 days
Runtime respects resolution policy and exposes explicit fallback reasons in logs and response diagnostics when fallback occurs
E2E tests cover common pin combos, ambiguous pins, and rollback scenarios; performance-regression < 2% p99 latency impact under typical workloads
technical_considerations: Pin types to support: commit-hash (40 hex), semver exact (1.2.3), semver-range (>=1.1 <2.0), tag (stable-2026-02), alias (e.g., 'recommended')
Resolution rules must be deterministic and independent of catalog ordering; implement canonical comparator in pin-resolver service
Store audit entries as append-only records with pin input, resolved_ref, resolver_version, timestamp, and operator (system|user) — surfaced via pin_audit_id
Avoid exploding catalog queries on each request: cache resolved_ref -> pin_audit_id for short TTL and invalidate on model publish events
Expose minimal diagnostics in public API (resolved_model_ref, pin_audit_id, fallback_reason) to avoid leaking internal implementation details

Edge case: semver-range that matches multiple published patch lines — resolver should pick highest semver that also satisfies performance-profile compatibility; tie-breaker: most recent publish timestamp
Performance profiles: binding must be explicit in audit entry (profile_id) so customers can correlate latency/cost expectations with the resolved model
Backwards compatibility: if no pin fields supplied, preserve current implicit resolution behavior; add feature flag to gate strict validation during rollout
api_changes: New admin endpoint: GET /v1/pins/{pin_audit_id} -> returns audit entry (immutable) for troubleshooting (RBAC protected)
Validation: 400 returned if client supplies malformed pin with strict validation enabled; otherwise warning code in diagnostics
sdk_changes: Add validate_pin() helper to Python/TS SDKs that checks format and returns a lint-style list of warnings/errors
Provide client-side resolver preview API (dry-run) that calls backend resolution but marks request as preview — useful in CI to detect future breakage
Surface pin_audit_id and pin_diagnostics on Response objects and ensure they are logged by default in SDK telemetry (opt-out controlled by config)
Expose constants/enums for pin types and SemVer helpers to avoid ad-hoc parsing in customer code
Docstrings and examples demonstrating safe pin patterns and migration from 'latest' alias to semver/commit pins
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Implement API + resolver changes behind feature flag; enable on internal org and 3 pilot customers; collect audit records and inspect discrepancies (2 weeks)
Phase 2 (sdk): Ship validate_pin() helper in Python/TS SDKs; warn-by-default in SDK when a non-explicit alias is used; release minor SDKs and migrate Redwood sample apps
Phase 3 (enforce): Offer strict server-side validation toggle to customers; default set to warn for 30 days then opt-in enforcement; communicate via Console banners
Phase 4 (GA): Promote feature flag to default for new routes, provide migration tooling to backfill pin_audit_id for existing pinned routes, and update docs
Rollback criteria: >3 customer tickets with unresolvable regressions or >1% increase in request error-rate attributable to pin logic -> revert feature flag and run hotfix
